translations.text: The chief eunuch gave them names: he called Daniel Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
Test your servants for ten days, and let us be given vegetables to eat and water to drink.
He agreed to their request and tested them for ten days.
But the angel of dew went down with Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael into the fiery furnace and drove the flame of fire out of the furnace.
Then all three, with one voice, praised and blessed God from inside the fiery furnace, saying:

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In your father's days, enlightenment, understanding, and great wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans.
This is the interpretation of the matter: Mene—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel—you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.

Then the officials and military commanders tried to find grounds for accusing Daniel concerning the affairs of the kingdom. But they could find no fault or grounds for accusation against him, because he was faithful to his God, and they found no wrongdoing or fault in him.

I issue a decree that throughout the dominion of my kingdom people must tremble and fear before Daniel's God. For he is the living God and endures forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his dominion lasts to the end.
An army was given authority over the regular offering because of sins. The sanctuary was thrown to the ground, and it advanced and prospered.
We have sinned, done wrong, acted wickedly, rebelled, and turned aside from your commandments and your judgments.

Lord, in keeping with all the righteous deeds you have done for us, let your anger and wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem and from your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the wrongdoing of our ancestors, your people have been scattered everywhere, and Jerusalem has become an object of scorn to all the nations.

My God, incline your ear and hear; open your eyes and see our ruins, our desolate places, and the city that bears your name. For we do not rely on our righteousness when we pray before you, but on your great mercy.

He will strengthen a covenant with many for one week, and for half a week he will put an end to sacrifice and offerings. On the wings of abomination will be destruction, until the full measure of what has been decreed comes to rest upon the destroyer.
At that time many will rise against the king of the north. Wicked men among your people will rise up to fulfill the vision, but they will be overthrown.

He will rouse his strength and courage against the king of the south with a large and powerful army. The king of the south will be stirred to battle with a large army and will become exceedingly strong, but he will not stand, because plots will be devised against him.
He will stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape his hands.

I heard the man dressed in splendid garments, who stood above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the hands of all the holy people are freed, all these things will be completed.
